stem: An inpatient psychiatric client repeatedly asks about exit locations and how visitor badges open doors. Which nursing action best addresses the identified elopement risk?

options.A: Continue routine observation until the client makes an actual exit attempt because questions about doors alone do not justify activating precautions.
options.B: Use the unit's elopement-risk process to implement preventive precautions appropriate to the assessed risk, such as enhanced observation and environmental or access controls.
options.C: Move the client closer to the nurses' station but leave the usual observation level unchanged because location alone is sufficient to manage the risk.
options.D: Document the concern and ask family to reinforce staying on the unit, but defer environmental precautions unless the client reaches an exit.

rationale: AHRQ PSNet describes elopement prevention as a combination of risk assessment and preventive precautions. For at-risk patients, precautions may include observation protocols and, in mental-health settings, environmental or access controls such as alarms or automatic door locks. B applies that principle without prescribing a single universal intervention. A and D wait for an actual attempt, while C relies on location alone rather than an appropriate risk-based precaution plan.
educational_objective: Respond to identified elopement risk with risk-based preventive precautions, including appropriate observation and environmental/access controls, rather than waiting for an actual exit attempt.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) PSNet
source_version_date: PSNet patient-safety commentary retained current; currentness rechecked against 2024 PSNet-indexed evidence

source_claim_supported: Patients should be assessed for elopement risk and at-risk patients placed on special preventive precautions; preventive measures may include enhanced observation and environmental/access controls appropriate to the setting.

source_original.stem: An inpatient psychiatric client repeatedly asks about exit locations and how visitor badges open doors. Which nursing action best addresses the identified elopement risk?

options.A: Continue routine observation until the client makes an actual exit attempt, because questions about doors alone do not justify activating elopement precautions.
options.B: Initiate the unit's elopement precautions based on the risk assessment, such as enhanced observation and appropriate control of access points and exits.
options.C: Move the client closer to the nurses' station but leave the usual observation level unchanged, because location alone is sufficient to manage the identified risk.
options.D: Document the elopement concern and ask family to reinforce staying on the unit, but defer environmental precautions unless the client reaches an exit.

source_original.rationale: AHRQ PSNet recommends assessment and preventive precautions for patients at elopement risk, including enhanced observation and environmental controls appropriate to the setting. Option B applies those measures after the concerning behavior is identified. Option A waits for an actual attempt before acting. Option C changes location but leaves the observation plan unchanged. Option D relies on documentation and family reinforcement while deferring precautions that address the identified safety risk.
source_original.source_detail: AHRQ PSNet — Elopement: identify elopement risk and implement preventive precautions appropriate to the setting, including observation protocols and environmental/access controls in behavioral-health settings. Current AHRQ PSNet elopement patient-safety guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15 against recent PSNet-indexed elopement literature. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: asepsis, equipment/environmental safety, incident/event prevention and infection-control activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key and construct but softened 'initiate the unit's elopement precautions' to 'use the unit's elopement-risk process' so the answer does not imply one universal protocol. Preventive observation/environmental controls remain directly source-supported.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Elopement risk prevention in inpatient psychiatry
audit_findings.source_authority: AHRQ PSNet patient-safety guidance plus current PSNet-indexed evidence.
audit_findings.currentness: Core commentary is older but retained; 2024 evidence remains consistent with risk evaluation and response algorithms.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Risk assessment, preventive precautions, observation/environmental controls, Take-Home Points.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No universal observation frequency, locking requirement or restraint intervention was invented.

distractor_audit.A: Waits for harm/attempt despite identified risk.
distractor_audit.C: Location alone is insufficient and leaves observation unchanged.
distractor_audit.D: Defers risk-control measures until an exit occurs.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B addresses the identified risk prospectively and comprehensively.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are plausible unit responses; no second defensible answer.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Confirmed the final wording remains policy-sensitive and does not overstate AHRQ examples as universal mandates.
